text:
akshay: quick heads-up — after the kernel-scheduler change (kernel-v2) i saw a burst of OOMs on canary around 03:10 UTC. pattern: lots of tiny streaming decode requests (2–8 tokens) and then a sharp workspace allocation spike.

jess: ouch. any flamegraphs or `dmesg`/logs to share?

rohit: putting a short profil run here — i captured allocator traces + kernel timings. gist: allocator hotpath time increased ~1.8x, and we see many ~6–12MB contiguous workspace requests that fail. small snippet:```
# sample workspace histogram (bytes):
[0-4KB]: 12k
[4KB-64KB]: 48k
[64KB-1MB]: 8k
[1MB-8MB]: 420
[8MB-32MB]: 72
# allocation latency percentiles (ms):
P50: 0.4 P95: 2.3 P99: 9.8
# kernel dispatch timings (decode path):
kernel-select v2 -> slightly better IPC, but increased workspace pressure on small-batch path
```

maria: my hunch: the kernel scheduling change prioritized fewer high-throughput kernels which increased prefill concurrency on the decode path and exposed fragmentation in the allocator. prefills are asking for contiguous KV slots for prefixes, which is killing the recycler ability to pack small slabs.

akshay: that matches what i see — majority of failures are `alloc_contig(>4MB)` in the same GPU under sustained small-batch bursts. also memory compaction is expensive at runtime.

jess: can we try two quick mitigations to validate root cause: 1) add a per-request soft cap for workspace (e.g., 8MB) that causes fallback to streaming decode, 2) slightly reduce prefill priority when concurrency > 64?

rohit: both are quick flags we can flip. i also want to test a scavenger pass that coalesces small free slabs periodically (cheap compaction). idea: allocator keeps free-lists per-slab-size and every N allocations run a lightweight coalesce. might reduce fragmentation without full compaction.

maria: agree. also propose an eviction tweak: when memory pressure is high, demote oldest KV prefixes rather than evicting arbitrary slices — demotion allows re-requesting prefix gradually instead of immediate decode path pressure. testing demotion threshold at 20% of pool freed.

perf-bot: perf microbench queued: `bench/kv_prefill_pressure --kernel-sched=v2 --prefill-prio=normal --per-request-cap=inf` and `...--per-request-cap=8MB --prefill-prio=low`. expected duration ~15m. link: https://ci.internal/2850012345/bench-results

akshay: plan: patch 1) flip per-request soft cap = 8MB (config-on-canary), patch 2) prefill prio degrade when concurrency>64, patch 3) enable scavenger coalesce (sampling every 10k allocs). run perf-bot bench and a 1h smoke. if green, roll to staging.

jess: i'll add tracepoints for alloc/release and kernel select decision so we can correlate scheduling events to OOMs. will also log `kv-demote` events. assigning to @jess, @rohit to run bench, @maria to add demotion policy draft.

rohit: on it. starting benchmark now. will paste preliminary numbers in ~20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: sketching demotion logic in a PR, will push comments early.

akshay: thanks. if this reproduces, we should also consider a longer-term change: kernel-sched needs a memory-awareness input (i.e., avoid scheduling many memory-hungry prefill kernels concurrently with low-latency decode kernels). but let's validate mitigations first. :+1:

perf-bot: bench complete — small snapshot:
 - baseline (no cap): 12 OOMs / 1h
 - per-request-cap=8MB + prefill-prio=low: 0 OOMs / 1h, median latency +1.2%
 - scavenger-coalesce enabled (sampling 1/10k): fragmentation metric down 18%
link: https://ci.internal/2850012345/bench-results/summary

jess: nice results. leaning to ship caps + prefill-prio change to staging. i'll open the rollout note and add canary guardrails.

akshay: deploy plan: canary config flip (flags) -> 2h observe -> if stable promote. keep demotion as follow-up PR to iterate.

maria: added initial demotion PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/allocator/pulls/4212 (WIP)

akshay: action items: 1) @jess add traces + rollout note, 2) @rohit run 4h bench and collect traces, 3) @maria polish demotion PR, 4) @perf-bot run daily regression under kernel-sched v2. we'll sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow morning if anything breaks.

jess: ack. thanks everyone! :rocket:
